signals.label: Review timing is uneven
signals.observed: 11 reviews fall within 7 days of 2026-03-06; about 0.9 would be expected if reviews were evenly spread across the 150 days.
signals.benign: A launch, restock, sale, or a popular video can genuinely produce a real spike of reviews.
signals.concern: Coordinated review campaigns also produce bursts that are dense and tightly packed.

signals.label: Repeated wording across reviews
signals.observed: 7 review pairs share at least 55% of their 5-word sequences; closest pair 100% similar.
signals.benign: People describing the same product often use the same natural phrases, especially for simple products.
signals.concern: Copy-paste templates and AI-generated reviews produce unusually similar text across different authors.

signals.label: Ratings cluster at five stars
signals.observed: 70% of 20 rated reviews are five stars; only 10% are one or two stars.
signals.benign: A genuinely excellent product sold to happy customers can legitimately have very few low ratings.
signals.concern: Inflation campaigns and suppression of negative reviews create the same shape.

signals.label: Several reviews share one author
signals.observed: Author "mira.k" appears 3 times (15% of all reviews).
signals.benign: Enthusiastic customers do write multiple reviews, and shared names are common.
signals.concern: A small set of accounts producing many reviews can indicate an organised campaign.

signals.label: Many reviews lack purchase verification
signals.observed: 40% of 20 reviews with verification data are marked unverified.
signals.benign: Some platforms do not verify purchases at all, and verified badges are not proof of honesty.
signals.concern: A high unverified share is one of the most cited signals in fake-review research.

signals.label: Some reviews lack concrete detail
signals.observed: 3 of 20 reviews are long but contain few measurements, product specifics, or first-hand details.
signals.benign: Short on detail is not the same as dishonest — many people simply write brief, emotional reviews.
signals.concern: Generated or template reviews often sound positive but describe no specific experience.

limits: These are observations, not verdicts. No review is declared fake or real.
We cannot verify who bought what, see IP addresses, or read private account history.
A benign explanation is shown for every signal — always read it before drawing a conclusion.
Confidence describes the strength of the measured pattern, not the probability of manipulation.
AI-written reviews may pass every statistical check. Substance signals reduce but do not remove this risk.
Results depend entirely on the data you provide; the tool never fetches reviews from any platform.
Each signal caps its displayed review IDs; the full exclusion set is exported as excludedIds.
